            raise CliExit(0)
        if arg.startswith('--') and len(arg) > 2:
            nameval = arg[2:]
            if '=' in nameval:
                name, value = nameval.split('=', 1)
                has_eq = True
            else:
                name, value = nameval, None
                has_eq = False
            if name not in LONG_SPECS:
                # A few close-match suggestions observed from clap.
                if name == "ver":
                    unexpected_arg(arg, usage="Usage: executable --version [FILE]", similar="--version")
                if name == "Style":
                    unexpected_arg(arg, usage="Usage: executable <FILE|--no-headers|--number|--tsv|--delimiter <DELIMITER>|--style <STYLE>|--padding <PADDING>|--indent <INDENT>|--sniff <LIMIT>|--header-align <HEADER_ALIGN>|--body-align <BODY_ALIGN>|--disable-pager>", similar="--style")
                if name == "no-header":
                    unexpected_arg(arg, usage="Usage: executable <FILE|--no-headers|--number|--tsv|--delimiter <DELIMITER>|--style <STYLE>|--padding <PADDING>|--indent <INDENT>|--sniff <LIMIT>|--header-align <HEADER_ALIGN>|--body-align <BODY_ALIGN>|--disable-pager>", similar="--no-headers")
                unexpected_arg(arg)
            kind, _ = LONG_SPECS[name]
            if kind == "help":
                sys.stdout.write(HELP_TEXT)
                raise CliExit(0)
            if kind == "version":
                sys.stdout.write(VERSION_TEXT)
                raise CliExit(0)
            if kind == "flag":
                if has_eq:
                    die2(f"error: unexpected value '{value}' for '{ARG_DISPLAY[name]}' found; no more were expected\n", usage=f"Usage: executable {ARG_DISPLAY[name]} [FILE]")
                set_option(opts, seen, name)
                i += 1
                continue
            # value option
            if has_eq:
                val = value
            else:
                val, i = get_following_value(argv, i, name)
            set_option(opts, seen, name, val)
            i += 1
            continue
        if arg.startswith('-') and arg != "-":
            # short options may be clustered. Options with values consume the rest
            # of the same token (optionally after '=') or the next argv item.
            j = 1
            while j < len(arg):
                ch = arg[j]
                if ch not in SHORT_SPECS:
                    unexpected_arg('-' + ch)
                canon = SHORT_SPECS[ch]
                if canon == "help":
                    sys.stdout.write(HELP_TEXT)
                    raise CliExit(0)
                if canon == "version":
                    sys.stdout.write(VERSION_TEXT)
                    raise CliExit(0)
                kind, _ = LONG_SPECS[canon]
                if kind == "flag":
                    set_option(opts, seen, canon)
                    j += 1
                    continue
                # value option: rest of token is the value; a leading '=' is stripped.
                if j + 1 < len(arg):
                    val = arg[j + 1:]
                    if val.startswith('='):
                        val = val[1:]
                    set_option(opts, seen, canon, val)
                    j = len(arg)
                    break
                else:
                    val, i = get_following_value(argv, i, canon)
                    set_option(opts, seen, canon, val)
                    j = len(arg)
                    break
            i += 1
            continue
        # positional file
        positionals.append(arg)
        i += 1
    if len(positionals) > 1:
        unexpected_arg(positionals[1], usage=usage_default())
    if positionals:
        opts.file = positionals[0]
    return opts

@dataclass
class Record:
    fields: list[bytes]
    line: int
    byte: int

class CsvError(Exception):
    pass

class CsvUtf8Error(Exception):
    def __init__(self, record_idx: int, line: int, byte: int, field_idx: int, near: int):
        self.record_idx = record_idx
        self.line = line
        self.byte = byte
        self.field_idx = field_idx
        self.near = near

class CsvFieldCountError(Exception):
    def __init__(self, record_idx: int, line: int, byte: int, fields: int, expected: int):
        self.record_idx = record_idx
        self.line = line
        self.byte = byte
        self.fields = fields
        self.expected = expected


def parse_csv_bytes(data: bytes, delim: int) -> list[Record]:
    records: list[Record] = []
    fields: list[bytes] = []
    cur = bytearray()
    in_quotes = False
    field_started = False
    record_started = False
    record_start_byte = 0
    record_start_line = 1
    line = 1
    i = 0
    n = len(data)

    def finish_record(end_i):
        nonlocal fields, cur, field_started, record_started, record_start_byte, record_start_line
        if (not record_started) and (not field_started) and len(cur) == 0 and len(fields) == 0:
            return False
        fields.append(bytes(cur))
        records.append(Record(fields, record_start_line, record_start_byte))
        fields = []
        cur = bytearray()
        field_started = False
        record_started = False
        return True

    while i < n:
        b = data[i]
        if in_quotes:
            if b == 0x22:  # quote
                if i + 1 < n and data[i + 1] == 0x22:
                    cur.append(0x22)
                    field_started = True
                    record_started = True
                    i += 2
                    continue
                else:
                    in_quotes = False
                    field_started = True
                    record_started = True
                    i += 1
                    continue
            else:
                cur.append(b)
                field_started = True
                record_started = True
                if b == 0x0A:
                    line += 1
                elif b == 0x0D:
                    # Treat CRLF in quoted fields as a single line break, preserving bytes.
                    if i + 1 < n and data[i + 1] == 0x0A:
                        cur.append(0x0A)
                        i += 1
                    line += 1
                i += 1
                continue
        else:
            if b == 0x22 and not field_started and len(cur) == 0:
                in_quotes = True
                field_started = True
                record_started = True
                i += 1
                continue
            if b == delim:
                fields.append(bytes(cur))
                cur = bytearray()
                field_started = False
                record_started = True
                i += 1
                continue
            if b == 0x0A or b == 0x0D:
                finish_record(i)
                if b == 0x0D and i + 1 < n and data[i + 1] == 0x0A:
                    i += 1
                line += 1
                i += 1
                record_start_byte = i
                record_start_line = line
                continue
            cur.append(b)
            field_started = True
            record_started = True
            i += 1
            continue
    # EOF: an open quote is accepted, and the accumulated field becomes a record.
    finish_record(n)
    return records


def decode_and_validate(records: list[Record]) -> list[list[str]]:
    out: list[list[str]] = []
    expected = None
    for idx, rec in enumerate(records):
        decoded: list[str] = []
        for fidx, raw in enumerate(rec.fields):
            try:
                decoded.append(raw.decode('utf-8'))
            except UnicodeDecodeError as e:
                raise CsvUtf8Error(idx, rec.line, rec.byte, fidx, e.start)
        if expected is None:
            expected = len(decoded)
        elif len(decoded) != expected:
            raise CsvFieldCountError(idx, rec.line, rec.byte, len(decoded), expected)
        out.append(decoded)
    return out

# --- Unicode display width and truncation ---

def _ord(ch):
    return ord(ch)

def is_variation_selector(ch: str) -> bool:
    cp = ord(ch)
    return 0xFE00 <= cp <= 0xFE0F or 0xE0100 <= cp <= 0xE01EF

def is_vs16(ch: str) -> bool:
    return ord(ch) == 0xFE0F

def is_emoji_modifier(ch: str) -> bool:
    cp = ord(ch)
    return 0x1F3FB <= cp <= 0x1F3FF

def is_regional_indicator(ch: str) -> bool:
    cp = ord(ch)
    return 0x1F1E6 <= cp <= 0x1F1FF

def is_keycap_mark(ch: str) -> bool:
    return ord(ch) == 0x20E3

def is_mark(ch: str) -> bool:
    return unicodedata.category(ch).startswith('M')

def is_zero_mark(ch: str) -> bool:
    # Nonspacing/enclosing marks have zero width. Spacing marks (Mc) are counted
    # by unicode-width and remain part of the grapheme cluster.
    return unicodedata.category(ch) in ('Mn', 'Me')

def is_emojiish(ch: str) -> bool:
    cp = ord(ch)
    return (
        0x1F000 <= cp <= 0x1FAFF or
        0x2600 <= cp <= 0x27BF
    )

def char_width(ch: str) -> int:
    cp = ord(ch)
    if ch == '\u200d':
        return 0
    if is_variation_selector(ch):
        return 0
    if is_emoji_modifier(ch):
        return 0
    if is_zero_mark(ch):
        return 0
    if is_keycap_mark(ch):
        return 0
    # The observed implementation counts ordinary controls, tabs and newlines as
    # one column for sizing purposes.
    if unicodedata.east_asian_width(ch) in ('W', 'F'):
        return 2
    return 1

def consume_marks(s: str, i: int) -> int:
    n = len(s)
    while i < n:
        ch = s[i]
        if is_mark(ch) or is_variation_selector(ch) or is_emoji_modifier(ch) or is_keycap_mark(ch):
            i += 1
        else:
            break
    return i

def cluster_width_plain(text: str) -> int:
    return sum(char_width(c) for c in text)

def iter_clusters(s: str):
    i = 0
    n = len(s)
    while i < n:
        ch = s[i]
        # Regional-indicator pairs form one flag cell of width two.
        if is_regional_indicator(ch) and i + 1 < n and is_regional_indicator(s[i + 1]):
            yield s[i:i+2], 2
            i += 2
            continue
        # Standalone combining/format marks: keep them as zero-width clusters.
        if is_mark(ch) or is_variation_selector(ch) or is_emoji_modifier(ch) or is_keycap_mark(ch):
            yield ch, char_width(ch)
            i += 1
            continue
        start = i
        i += 1
        i = consume_marks(s, i)
        text = s[start:i]
        has_vs16 = any(is_vs16(c) for c in text)
        has_keycap = any(is_keycap_mark(c) for c in text)
        emoji_seq = (is_emojiish(ch) or has_vs16 or has_keycap)
        # Emoji presentation and keycap sequences occupy two columns even if the
        # base symbol (heart, snowman, digit, etc.) is otherwise narrow.
        if has_vs16 or has_keycap:
            width = 2
        else:
            width = cluster_width_plain(text)
        # Emoji ZWJ sequences are a single two-column grapheme in unicode-width.
        if emoji_seq:
            while i < n and s[i] == '\u200d' and i + 1 < n:
                j = i + 1
                base = s[j]
                j += 1
                j = consume_marks(s, j)
                text += s[i:j]
                i = j
                width = 2
                emoji_seq = True
        yield text, width

def display_width(s: str) -> int:
    return sum(w for _, w in iter_clusters(s))

def truncate_to_width(s: str, max_width: int) -> str:
    if max_width < 0:
        max_width = 0
    used = 0
    parts = []
    for text, w in iter_clusters(s):
        if used + w > max_width:
            break
        parts.append(text)
        used += w
    return ''.join(parts)

def make_hline(widths: list[int], padding: int, cfg_tuple) -> str:
    left, sep, right, horiz = cfg_tuple
    segs = [horiz * (w + 2 * padding) for w in widths]
    return left + sep.join(segs) + right

def format_cell(text: str, width: int, align: str, padding: int) -> str:
    text = truncate_to_width(text, width)
    w = display_width(text)
    extra = width - w
    if extra < 0:
        extra = 0
    if align == "right":
        left_extra, right_extra = extra, 0
    elif align == "center":
        left_extra = extra // 2
        right_extra = extra - left_extra
    else:
        left_extra, right_extra = 0, extra
    return " " * padding + " " * left_extra + text + " " * right_extra + " " * padding

def make_row(row: list[str], widths: list[int], align: str, padding: int, style: str) -> str:
    left, sep, right = STYLE_CFG[style]["row"]
    cells = [format_cell(row[i] if i < len(row) else "", widths[i], align, padding) for i in range(len(widths))]
    return left + sep.join(cells) + right

def render_table(header: list[str] | None, body: list[list[str]], opts: Options, ncols: int) -> str:
    widths = [0] * ncols
    if opts.number and ncols > 0:
        widths[0] = max(widths[0], 1)

    width_rows: list[list[str]] = []
    if header is not None:
        width_rows.append(header)
    if opts.sniff == 0:
        width_rows.extend(body)
    else:
        width_rows.extend(body[:opts.sniff])
    for row in width_rows:
        for i in range(min(len(row), ncols)):
            w = display_width(row[i])
            if w > widths[i]:
                widths[i] = w

    logical: list[tuple[str, list[str]]] = []
    if header is not None:
        logical.append(("header", header))
    for row in body:
        logical.append(("body", row))

    style = opts.style
    cfg = STYLE_CFG[style]
    indent = " " * opts.indent
    lines: list[str] = []
    def add(line: str):
        lines.append(indent + line + "\n")

    if not logical:
        if cfg["top"] is not None:
            add(make_hline(widths, opts.padding, cfg["top"]))
            add(make_hline(widths, opts.padding, cfg["bottom"]))
        return ''.join(lines)

    if cfg["top"] is not None:
        add(make_hline(widths, opts.padding, cfg["top"]))

    for idx, (kind, row) in enumerate(logical):
        align = opts.header_align if kind == "header" else opts.body_align
        add(make_row(row, widths, align, opts.padding, style))
        if idx != len(logical) - 1:
            need_sep = False
            if style == "grid":
                need_sep = True
            elif kind == "header" and cfg["mid"] is not None:
                need_sep = True
            if need_sep:
                add(make_hline(widths, opts.padding, cfg["mid"]))

    if cfg["bottom"] is not None:
        add(make_hline(widths, opts.padding, cfg["bottom"]))
    return ''.join(lines)


def build_rows(records: list[list[str]], opts: Options):
    if opts.no_headers:
        header = None
        body = [list(r) for r in records]
        base_cols = len(records[0]) if records else 0
    else:
        if records:
            header = list(records[0])
            body = [list(r) for r in records[1:]]
            base_cols = len(header)
        else:
            header = []
            body = []
            base_cols = 0
    if opts.number:
        if header is not None:
            header = ["#"] + header
            body = [[str(i + 1)] + row for i, row in enumerate(body)]
        else:
            body = [[str(i + 1)] + row for i, row in enumerate(body)]
        ncols = base_cols + 1
    else:
        ncols = base_cols
    return header, body, ncols


def read_input(opts: Options) -> bytes:
    if opts.file is None:
        return sys.stdin.buffer.read()
    try:
        with open(opts.file, 'rb') as f:
            return f.read()
    except OSError as e:
        # Rust's std::io error Display uses this compact form.
        sys.stderr.write(f"csview: {e.strerror} (os error {e.errno})\n")
        raise CliExit(1)


def delimiter_byte(delim_char: str) -> int:
    # The observed tool accepts a Rust char and passes it as a single byte; this
    # is equivalent to truncating the Unicode scalar value to u8.
    return ord(delim_char) & 0xFF


def run(argv) -> int:
    try:
        opts = parse_args(argv)
        data = read_input(opts)
        records_meta = parse_csv_bytes(data, delimiter_byte(opts.delimiter))
        try:
            records = decode_and_validate(records_meta)
        except CsvUtf8Error as e:
            sys.stderr.write(
                f"csview: CSV parse error: record {e.record_idx} (line {e.line}, field: {e.field_idx}, byte: {e.byte}): "
                f"invalid utf-8: invalid UTF-8 in field {e.field_idx} near byte index {e.near}\n"
            )
            return 1
        except CsvFieldCountError as e:
            sys.stderr.write(
                f"csview: CSV error: record {e.record_idx} (line: {e.line}, byte: {e.byte}): "
                f"found record with {e.fields} fields, but the previous record has {e.expected} fields\n"
            )
            return 1
        header, body, ncols = build_rows(records, opts)
        sys.stdout.write(render_table(header, body, opts, ncols))
        return 0
    except CliExit as e:
        return e.code

if __name__ == '__main__':
    sys.exit(run(sys.argv[1:]))

        msg += f": {detail}"
    msg += "\n"
    possible = ""
    if canon == "style":
        possible = STYLE_POSSIBLE
    elif canon in ("header-align", "body-align"):
        possible = ALIGN_POSSIBLE
    die2(msg, possible=possible)

def parse_uint_value(canon: str, value: str) -> int:
    # Rust's usize parser reports this same generic message for signs and bad digits.
    if value == "" or any(ch < '0' or ch > '9' for ch in value):
        invalid_value(canon, value, "invalid digit found in string")
    try:
        return int(value, 10)
    except Exception:
        invalid_value(canon, value, "invalid digit found in string")
    return 0

def parse_delimiter(value: str) -> str:
    if len(value) == 0:
        invalid_value("delimiter", value, "cannot parse char from empty string")
    # Rust char parsing counts Unicode scalar values, not UTF-8 bytes.
    if len(value) != 1:
        invalid_value("delimiter", value, "too many characters in string")
    return value

def normalize_enum(canon: str, value: str) -> str:
    low = value.lower()
    if canon == "style":
        if low not in STYLE_VALUES:
            invalid_value(canon, value)
        return low
    if canon in ("header-align", "body-align"):
        if low not in ALIGN_VALUES:
            invalid_value(canon, value)
        return low
    return value

def set_option(opts: Options, seen: set[str], canon: str, raw_value: str | None = None):
    if canon in seen:
        duplicate_arg(canon)
    # Conflict is reported when the second of the pair is seen.
    if canon == "tsv" and "delimiter" in seen:
        conflict_arg("tsv", "delimiter")
    if canon == "delimiter" and "tsv" in seen:
        conflict_arg("delimiter", "tsv")
    seen.add(canon)

    kind, attr = LONG_SPECS[canon]
    if kind == "flag":
        setattr(opts, attr, True)
        if canon == "tsv":
            opts.delimiter = "\t"
    elif kind == "value":
        assert raw_value is not None
        if canon == "delimiter":
            opts.delimiter = parse_delimiter(raw_value)
        elif canon == "style":
            opts.style = normalize_enum(canon, raw_value)
        elif canon == "padding":
            opts.padding = parse_uint_value(canon, raw_value)
        elif canon == "indent":
            opts.indent = parse_uint_value(canon, raw_value)
        elif canon == "sniff":
            opts.sniff = parse_uint_value(canon, raw_value)
        elif canon == "header-align":
            opts.header_align = normalize_enum(canon, raw_value)
        elif canon == "body-align":
            opts.body_align = normalize_enum(canon, raw_value)

def looks_like_option(s: str) -> bool:
    return len(s) > 1 and s.startswith('-')

def get_following_value(args, i: int, canon: str):
    if i + 1 >= len(args):
        missing_value(canon)
    nxt = args[i + 1]
    if nxt == "--":
        missing_value(canon)
    # clap accepts a lone '-' as a value, but treats -x/-1/--foo as an option token.
    if looks_like_option(nxt):
        # Numeric-looking negative values are reported as unexpected arguments by clap
        # for integer options. Unknown short option tokens are likewise unexpected.
        if canon in ("padding", "indent", "sniff") and len(nxt) > 1 and nxt[1].isdigit():
            unexpected_arg(nxt)
        if nxt in ("-h", "--help", "-V", "--version") or nxt.startswith('--'):
            missing_value(canon)
        if nxt.startswith('-') and len(nxt) > 1:
            unexpected_arg(nxt)
    return nxt, i + 1

def parse_args(argv) -> Options:
    opts = Options()
    seen: set[str] = set()
    positionals = []
    i = 0
    positional_mode = False
    while i < len(argv):
        arg = argv[i]
        if positional_mode:
            positionals.append(arg)
            i += 1
            continue
        if arg == "--":
            positional_mode = True
            i += 1
            continue
        if arg == "--help":
            sys.stdout.write(HELP_TEXT)
            raise CliExit(0)
        if arg == "--version":
            sys.stdout.write(VERSION_TEXT)
            raise CliExit(0)
        if arg.startswith('--') and len(arg) > 2:
            nameval = arg[2:]
            if '=' in nameval:
                name, value = nameval.split('=', 1)
                has_eq = True
            else:
                name, value = nameval, None
                has_eq = False
            if name not in LONG_SPECS:
                # A few close-match suggestions observed from clap.
                if name == "ver":
                    unexpected_arg(arg, usage="Usage: executable --version [FILE]", similar="--version")
                if name == "Style":
                    unexpected_arg(arg, usage="Usage: executable <FILE|--no-headers|--number|--tsv|--delimiter <DELIMITER>|--style <STYLE>|--padding <PADDING>|--indent <INDENT>|--sniff <LIMIT>|--header-align <HEADER_ALIGN>|--body-align <BODY_ALIGN>|--disable-pager>", similar="--style")
                if name == "no-header":
                    unexpected_arg(arg, usage="Usage: executable <FILE|--no-headers|--number|--tsv|--delimiter <DELIMITER>|--style <STYLE>|--padding <PADDING>|--indent <INDENT>|--sniff <LIMIT>|--header-align <HEADER_ALIGN>|--body-align <BODY_ALIGN>|--disable-pager>", similar="--no-headers")
                unexpected_arg(arg)
            kind, _ = LONG_SPECS[name]
            if kind == "help":
                sys.stdout.write(HELP_TEXT)
                raise CliExit(0)
            if kind == "version":
                sys.stdout.write(VERSION_TEXT)
                raise CliExit(0)
            if kind == "flag":
                if has_eq:
                    die2(f"error: unexpected value '{value}' for '{ARG_DISPLAY[name]}' found; no more were expected\n", usage=f"Usage: executable {ARG_DISPLAY[name]} [FILE]")
                set_option(opts, seen, name)
                i += 1
                continue
            # value option
            if has_eq:
                val = value
            else:
                val, i = get_following_value(argv, i, name)
            set_option(opts, seen, name, val)
            i += 1
            continue
        if arg.startswith('-') and arg != "-":
            # short options may be clustered. Options with values consume the rest
            # of the same token (optionally after '=') or the next argv item.
            j = 1
            while j < len(arg):
                ch = arg[j]
                if ch not in SHORT_SPECS:
                    unexpected_arg('-' + ch)
                canon = SHORT_SPECS[ch]
                if canon == "help":
                    sys.stdout.write(HELP_TEXT)
                    raise CliExit(0)
                if canon == "version":
                    sys.stdout.write(VERSION_TEXT)
                    raise CliExit(0)
                kind, _ = LONG_SPECS[canon]
                if kind == "flag":
                    set_option(opts, seen, canon)
                    j += 1
                    continue
                # value option: rest of token is the value; a leading '=' is stripped.
                if j + 1 < len(arg):
                    val = arg[j + 1:]
                    if val.startswith('='):
                        val = val[1:]
                    set_option(opts, seen, canon, val)
                    j = len(arg)
                    break
                else:
                    val, i = get_following_value(argv, i, canon)
                    set_option(opts, seen, canon, val)
                    j = len(arg)
                    break
            i += 1
            continue
        # positional file
        positionals.append(arg)
        i += 1
    if len(positionals) > 1:
        unexpected_arg(positionals[1], usage=usage_default())
    if positionals:
        opts.file = positionals[0]
    return opts

@dataclass
class Record:
    fields: list[bytes]
    line: int
    byte: int

class CsvError(Exception):
    pass

class CsvUtf8Error(Exception):
    def __init__(self, record_idx: int, line: int, byte: int, field_idx: int, near: int):
        self.record_idx = record_idx
        self.line = line
        self.byte = byte
        self.field_idx = field_idx
        self.near = near

class CsvFieldCountError(Exception):
    def __init__(self, record_idx: int, line: int, byte: int, fields: int, expected: int):
        self.record_idx = record_idx
        self.line = line
        self.byte = byte
        self.fields = fields
        self.expected = expected


def parse_csv_bytes(data: bytes, delim: int) -> list[Record]:
    records: list[Record] = []
    fields: list[bytes] = []
    cur = bytearray()
    in_quotes = False
    field_started = False
    record_started = False
    record_start_byte = 0
    record_start_line = 1
    line = 1
    i = 0
    n = len(data)

    def finish_record(end_i):
        nonlocal fields, cur, field_started, record_started, record_start_byte, record_start_line
        if (not record_started) and (not field_started) and len(cur) == 0 and len(fields) == 0:
            return False
        fields.append(bytes(cur))
        records.append(Record(fields, record_start_line, record_start_byte))
        fields = []
        cur = bytearray()
        field_started = False
        record_started = False
        return True

    while i < n:
        b = data[i]
        if in_quotes:
            if b == 0x22:  # quote
                if i + 1 < n and data[i + 1] == 0x22:
                    cur.append(0x22)
                    field_started = True
                    record_started = True
                    i += 2
                    continue
                else:
                    in_quotes = False
                    field_started = True
                    record_started = True
                    i += 1
                    continue
            else:
                cur.append(b)
                field_started = True
                record_started = True
                if b == 0x0A:
                    line += 1
                elif b == 0x0D:
                    # Treat CRLF in quoted fields as a single line break, preserving bytes.
                    if i + 1 < n and data[i + 1] == 0x0A:
                        cur.append(0x0A)
                        i += 1
                    line += 1
                i += 1
                continue
        else:
            if b == 0x22 and not field_started and len(cur) == 0:
                in_quotes = True
                field_started = True
                record_started = True
                i += 1
                continue
            if b == delim:
                fields.append(bytes(cur))
                cur = bytearray()
                field_started = False
                record_started = True
                i += 1
                continue
            if b == 0x0A or b == 0x0D:
                finish_record(i)
                if b == 0x0D and i + 1 < n and data[i + 1] == 0x0A:
                    i += 1
                line += 1
                i += 1
                record_start_byte = i
                record_start_line = line
                continue
            cur.append(b)
            field_started = True
            record_started = True
            i += 1
            continue
    # EOF: an open quote is accepted, and the accumulated field becomes a record.
    finish_record(n)
    return records


def decode_and_validate(records: list[Record]) -> list[list[str]]:
    out: list[list[str]] = []
    expected = None
    for idx, rec in enumerate(records):
        decoded: list[str] = []
        for fidx, raw in enumerate(rec.fields):
            try:
                decoded.append(raw.decode('utf-8'))
            except UnicodeDecodeError as e:
                raise CsvUtf8Error(idx, rec.line, rec.byte, fidx, e.start)
        if expected is None:
            expected = len(decoded)
        elif len(decoded) != expected:
            raise CsvFieldCountError(idx, rec.line, rec.byte, len(decoded), expected)
        out.append(decoded)
    return out

# --- Unicode display width and truncation ---

def _ord(ch):
    return ord(ch)

def is_variation_selector(ch: str) -> bool:
    cp = ord(ch)
    return 0xFE00 <= cp <= 0xFE0F or 0xE0100 <= cp <= 0xE01EF

def is_vs16(ch: str) -> bool:
    return ord(ch) == 0xFE0F

def is_emoji_modifier(ch: str) -> bool:
    cp = ord(ch)
    return 0x1F3FB <= cp <= 0x1F3FF

def is_regional_indicator(ch: str) -> bool:
    cp = ord(ch)
    return 0x1F1E6 <= cp <= 0x1F1FF

def is_keycap_mark(ch: str) -> bool:
    return ord(ch) == 0x20E3

def is_mark(ch: str) -> bool:
    return unicodedata.category(ch).startswith('M')

def is_zero_mark(ch: str) -> bool:
    # Nonspacing/enclosing marks have zero width. Spacing marks (Mc) are counted
    # by unicode-width and remain part of the grapheme cluster.
    return unicodedata.category(ch) in ('Mn', 'Me')

def is_emojiish(ch: str) -> bool:
    cp = ord(ch)
    return (
        0x1F000 <= cp <= 0x1FAFF or
        0x2600 <= cp <= 0x27BF
    )

def char_width(ch: str) -> int:
    cp = ord(ch)
    if ch == '\u200d':
        return 0
    if is_variation_selector(ch):
        return 0
    if is_emoji_modifier(ch):
        return 0
    if is_zero_mark(ch):
        return 0
    if is_keycap_mark(ch):
        return 0
    # The observed implementation counts ordinary controls, tabs and newlines as
    # one column for sizing purposes.
    if unicodedata.east_asian_width(ch) in ('W', 'F'):
        return 2
    return 1

def consume_marks(s: str, i: int) -> int:
    n = len(s)
    while i < n:
        ch = s[i]
        if is_mark(ch) or is_variation_selector(ch) or is_emoji_modifier(ch) or is_keycap_mark(ch):
            i += 1
        else:
            break
    return i

def cluster_width_plain(text: str) -> int:
    return sum(char_width(c) for c in text)

def iter_clusters(s: str):
    i = 0
    n = len(s)
    while i < n:
        ch = s[i]
        # Regional-indicator pairs form one flag cell of width two.
        if is_regional_indicator(ch) and i + 1 < n and is_regional_indicator(s[i + 1]):
            yield s[i:i+2], 2
            i += 2
            continue
        # Standalone combining/format marks: keep them as zero-width clusters.
        if is_mark(ch) or is_variation_selector(ch) or is_emoji_modifier(ch) or is_keycap_mark(ch):
            yield ch, char_width(ch)
            i += 1
            continue
        start = i
        i += 1
        i = consume_marks(s, i)
        text = s[start:i]
        has_vs16 = any(is_vs16(c) for c in text)
        has_keycap = any(is_keycap_mark(c) for c in text)
        emoji_seq = (is_emojiish(ch) or has_vs16 or has_keycap)
        # Emoji presentation and keycap sequences occupy two columns even if the
        # base symbol (heart, snowman, digit, etc.) is otherwise narrow.
        if has_vs16 or has_keycap:
            width = 2
        else:
            width = cluster_width_plain(text)
        # Emoji ZWJ sequences are a single two-column grapheme in unicode-width.
        if emoji_seq:
            while i < n and s[i] == '\u200d' and i + 1 < n:
                j = i + 1
                base = s[j]
                j += 1
                j = consume_marks(s, j)
                text += s[i:j]
                i = j
                width = 2
                emoji_seq = True
        yield text, width

def display_width(s: str) -> int:
    return sum(w for _, w in iter_clusters(s))

def truncate_to_width(s: str, max_width: int) -> str:
    if max_width < 0:
        max_width = 0
    used = 0
    parts = []
    for text, w in iter_clusters(s):
        if used + w > max_width:
            break
        parts.append(text)
        used += w
    return ''.join(parts)

def make_hline(widths: list[int], padding: int, cfg_tuple) -> str:
    left, sep, right, horiz = cfg_tuple
    segs = [horiz * (w + 2 * padding) for w in widths]
    return left + sep.join(segs) + right

def format_cell(text: str, width: int, align: str, padding: int) -> str:
    text = truncate_to_width(text, width)
    w = display_width(text)
    extra = width - w
    if extra < 0:
        extra = 0
    if align == "right":
        left_extra, right_extra = extra, 0
    elif align == "center":
        left_extra = extra // 2
        right_extra = extra - left_extra
    else:
        left_extra, right_extra = 0, extra
    return " " * padding + " " * left_extra + text + " " * right_extra + " " * padding

def make_row(row: list[str], widths: list[int], align: str, padding: int, style: str) -> str:
    left, sep, right = STYLE_CFG[style]["row"]
    cells = [format_cell(row[i] if i < len(row) else "", widths[i], align, padding) for i in range(len(widths))]
    return left + sep.join(cells) + right

def render_table(header: list[str] | None, body: list[list[str]], opts: Options, ncols: int) -> str:
    widths = [0] * ncols
    if opts.number and ncols > 0:
        widths[0] = max(widths[0], 1)

    width_rows: list[list[str]] = []
    if header is not None:
        width_rows.append(header)
    if opts.sniff == 0:
        width_rows.extend(body)
    else:
        width_rows.extend(body[:opts.sniff])
    for row in width_rows:
        for i in range(min(len(row), ncols)):
            w = display_width(row[i])
            if w > widths[i]:
                widths[i] = w

    logical: list[tuple[str, list[str]]] = []
    if header is not None:
        logical.append(("header", header))
    for row in body:
        logical.append(("body", row))

    style = opts.style
    cfg = STYLE_CFG[style]
    indent = " " * opts.indent
    lines: list[str] = []
    def add(line: str):
        lines.append(indent + line + "\n")

    if not logical:
        if cfg["top"] is not None:
            add(make_hline(widths, opts.padding, cfg["top"]))
            add(make_hline(widths, opts.padding, cfg["bottom"]))
        return ''.join(lines)

    if cfg["top"] is not None:
        add(make_hline(widths, opts.padding, cfg["top"]))

    for idx, (kind, row) in enumerate(logical):
        align = opts.header_align if kind == "header" else opts.body_align
        add(make_row(row, widths, align, opts.padding, style))
        if idx != len(logical) - 1:
            need_sep = False
            if style == "grid":
                need_sep = True
            elif kind == "header" and cfg["mid"] is not None:
                need_sep = True
            if need_sep:
                add(make_hline(widths, opts.padding, cfg["mid"]))

    if cfg["bottom"] is not None:
        add(make_hline(widths, opts.padding, cfg["bottom"]))
    return ''.join(lines)


def build_rows(records: list[list[str]], opts: Options):
    if opts.no_headers:
        header = None
        body = [list(r) for r in records]
        base_cols = len(records[0]) if records else 0
    else:
        if records:
            header = list(records[0])
            body = [list(r) for r in records[1:]]
            base_cols = len(header)
        else:
            header = []
            body = []
            base_cols = 0
    if opts.number:
        if header is not None:
            header = ["#"] + header
            body = [[str(i + 1)] + row for i, row in enumerate(body)]
        else:
            body = [[str(i + 1)] + row for i, row in enumerate(body)]
        ncols = base_cols + 1
    else:
        ncols = base_cols
    return header, body, ncols


def read_input(opts: Options) -> bytes:
    if opts.file is None:
        return sys.stdin.buffer.read()
    try:
        with open(opts.file, 'rb') as f:
            return f.read()
    except OSError as e:
        # Rust's std::io error Display uses this compact form.
        sys.stderr.write(f"csview: {e.strerror} (os error {e.errno})\n")
        raise CliExit(1)


def delimiter_byte(delim_char: str) -> int:
    # The observed tool accepts a Rust char and passes it as a single byte; this
    # is equivalent to truncating the Unicode scalar value to u8.
    return ord(delim_char) & 0xFF


def run(argv) -> int:
    try:
        opts = parse_args(argv)
        data = read_input(opts)
        records_meta = parse_csv_bytes(data, delimiter_byte(opts.delimiter))
        try:
            records = decode_and_validate(records_meta)
        except CsvUtf8Error as e:
            sys.stderr.write(
                f"csview: CSV parse error: record {e.record_idx} (line {e.line}, field: {e.field_idx}, byte: {e.byte}): "
                f"invalid utf-8: invalid UTF-8 in field {e.field_idx} near byte index {e.near}\n"
            )
            return 1
        except CsvFieldCountError as e:
            sys.stderr.write(
                f"csview: CSV error: record {e.record_idx} (line: {e.line}, byte: {e.byte}): "
                f"found record with {e.fields} fields, but the previous record has {e.expected} fields\n"
            )
            return 1
        header, body, ncols = build_rows(records, opts)
        sys.stdout.write(render_table(header, body, opts, ncols))
        return 0
    except CliExit as e:
        return e.code

if __name__ == '__main__':
    sys.exit(run(sys.argv[1:]))
